issues.description: The supplied ZIP contains code and documentation but no required raw Call Report schedules, regulator index, TED file, SOD/HPI files, RIE inputs, POR files, or author-generated final sample. The code consumes several different local formats and exact key/field layouts. Public sources document candidate products, but the code-compatible vintages, formats, and required fields are not verified.

The code header describes WRDS 2000Q1–2010Q4 while the datasheet says 2001Q1–2010Q4, followed by FFIEC 2010Q1–2012Q4. Construction filters use quarter<200 and quarter>199, while analysis filters use quarter>163 without a terminal cap. TED uses four-quarter leads/lags, HPI builds four-quarter forward/backward ratios, and late-call-date input files stop at 2010Q4. Exact estimation endpoints and the full supporting raw history (including the HPI forward window) are not reconciled.

alst_cross_states.dta is merged in both the main analysis and independent Figure 6 branch using rssd9200 and index b, but no import or cleaning producer appears in code.do. The author page identifies a state-level index and download link, but the file schema, uniqueness and preparation into the required Stata file remain unverified.

The RIE loop reads ../filelist.txt and imports every listed file; neither the manifest nor its producer is included. The actual date coverage and file-name contract therefore remain unknown, in addition to the separately enumerated dated RIE files.

The source sets author-specific absolute Dropbox roots and writes to several relative and nested output directories. A host-visible [redacted-path-59bf254f867f] root and writable directory tree are not configured here. The two root resets themselves are coherent: B saves Data/work files/sample and C reads that same file from the parent root.

Five invoked Stata community commands (outtable, outreg2, winsor2, eqprhistogram and fastxtile) were not found by their same-runtime Stata 18 command probes and need to be located or installed from an approved source.

evidence.quote:
2.1) The Reports of Condition and Income (Call Report) Dataset used in his project was
downloaded from the Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS) on August 17th, 2013 and it
covers the 2001:Q1–2010:Q4 period. On September 19, 2013, we downloaded supplemental
call report data from the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC) to
cover the period 2010:Q1–2012:Q4.
2.2) The State Level U.S. Banking Regulatory Index based on Agarwal, Lucca, Seru, and
Trebbi, Quarterly Journal of Economics, 2014 was sent to us by Amit Seru on an email dated
July 22nd, 2014. The dataset is currently publicly available at Amit Seru’s personal website
at Stanford University (https://people.stanford.edu/aseru/data-and-discussions).
2.3) TED Spread data was retrieved from the FRED website maintained by the Federal
Reserve of St. Louis on July 24th, 2014.
2.4) House Price data is obtained from the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) website
on January 23rd, 2014. We merged the house price index data obtained from the FHFA with
Summary of Deposits data obtained from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC)
to create an index of the exposure of each bank to house price changes.

import delimited "TEDRATE.csv", clear

replace q = "2" if q=="04"
replace q = "3" if q=="07"
replace q = "4" if q=="10"
gen y = substr(date,1,4)
destring q y date, replace force
gen quarter = yq(y,q)
drop y q date

tsset quarter
gen nextyr_av_ted = f4.av_ted
gen lastyr_av_ted = l4.av_ted

egen fr = mode(FedReg), by(rssd9001)
replace FedReg = fr if FedReg==. 
drop fr

egen cnty = mode(county), by(rssd9001)
replace county = cnty if county==.
drop cnty
drop cnty_qt
egen cnty_qt = group(county quarter)
 
//Merging the Bank Regulatory Index
merge m:1 rssd9200 using "$dropbox/Data/cleaned files/alst_cross_states"
replace b = 0 if FedReg==1 & b!=.
drop _merge


tsset rssd9001 quarter
gen prov_ratio = prov_qrt/tot_loans
gen coratio =  CO_qrt/tot_loans
gen ALLLratio = riad3123/tot_loans

winsor2 prov_ratio coratio ALLLratio, replace cuts(2.5 97.5) trim

winsor2 totass, replace cuts(1 99) 
replace totass=ln(totass)
replace totdep=ln(totdep)

global c totass totdep resishare creshare oreo_ratio commit_ratio cshare wellcap

// 4 Leads and 4 Lags

preserve
areg prov_ratio c.b#i.quarter f1.coratio f2.coratio f3.coratio coratio l.coratio l2.coratio l3.coratio l4.coratio $c i.FedReg  if quarter>163, absorb(cnty_qt) vce(cl reg_state)
putexcel set "regcoefs.xls", replace
matrix A1 = e(b)
matrix A1 = A1[1,1..46]
matrix A1 = A1'
matrix B1 = vecdiag(e(V))
matrix B1 = B1[1,1..46]
matrix B1 = B1'

putexcel A1=matrix(A1)
putexcel B1=matrix(B1)

import excel "regcoefs.xls", sheet("Sheet1") clear
gen sterror = (B^.5)
gen ll = A - sterror*1.645

dependency_review.description: These are the 25 named WRDS-era RCON/RCFD schedule inputs used by the bank-quarter construction; code cites the schedule stems and selects actual column fields in the surrounding source.
SOD_all.dta is directly read to merge branch geography and deposit weights into the four quarterly bank-specific HPI files.
RIE_data.dta is generated by appending the filelist-driven quarterly RIE inputs and the separately enumerated dated RIE schedule files.
TEDRATE.csv is the required source used to create quarterly av_ted and its four-quarter leads/lags.
The named CBSA HPI CSV supplies the metropolitan-area HPI series.
The named workbook supplies state nonmetropolitan HPI values used in the geography merge.
The named Puerto Rico HPI workbook supplies the PR series appended to the state nonmetropolitan series.
The fixed-date Call Schedule RIE text files are explicitly imported and appended to the dynamic RIE input.
The listed Call Bulk POR text files supply submission dates used to construct late-amendment indicators.
regcoefs.xls is written from estimation matrices via putexcel and immediately imported for Figure 6; it is not a packaged spreadsheet input.
RSSD is read as the bank identity/regulatory/geography source that produces regmaster.
RIAD is read as the income-statement and loan-loss source used to produce char.
Both references point to the regmaster dataset created from RSSD in A.0.1 and reloaded by B and the independent Figure 6 branch; the differing Dropbox roots resolve to the same Data tree.
RC.dta is the base dataset for the FFIEC-era call-report schedule merge.
var1994_2010 is a temporary panel built by merging regmaster with RIAD and RCON/RCFD schedules and retaining the pre-2010 branch.
days12312010 is created by the POR import loop and serves as the seed for the combined dates panel.
work files/sample is the generated merged bank-quarter panel consumed by the published-paper tables/figures and the Figure 6 companion.
Temporary datasets `a` and `r` are saved from the in-memory generated sample and reloaded for the subgroup statistics and Table 2 model branch.
error_temp is one of the temporary restatement-category files generated in the Table 1 Panel C reshape loop.

steps: Confirm the intended older Call Report source window against the code comment, datasheet and quarter filters; document the 2010Q1 WRDS/FFIEC handoff and target sample endpoint.
Obtain the author-described RSSD, RIAD and RCON/RCFD schedule .dta files if available, or document a compatible official bulk-data-to-Stata preparation route for the required quarter/schedule fields.
Stage the FFIEC-era RC.dta and every schedule named in local d, preserving the source quarter keys and field mappings; no downstream variable definitions should be replaced.
Keep the code’s source branches and merge/update behavior intact while resolving the raw file vintages and any duplicate bank-quarter handling.
validation: Check each expected input filename and field against its actual source layout.
Validate rssd9001-quarter keys, input history, cross-source boundary and 2010Q1–2012Q4 FFIEC coverage before a separately authorized execution.

actions.description: Obtain and prepare the state-level regulatory index in the exact format consumed by both analyses.
steps: Retrieve or identify the author-linked State Level index file and its documentation.
Verify the columns rssd9200 and b, the key uniqueness expected by the m:1 merges, and how the 1996–2011 index period maps to the analysis sample.
Prepare alst_cross_states.dta under the configured cleaned-files directory only after confirming the author file’s field mapping; preserve the FedReg replacement rule in code.do.
validation: Confirm the prepared file and rssd9200 key against both merge sites before any authorized run.

Recover the author’s quarterly observation rule or other documented conversion that matches the one-row-per-quarter input expected by code.do; do not assume a quarterly mean or choose a different series.
Map the selected series to date and tedrate, retain the required lead/lag window, and save the expected TEDRATE.csv/cleaned TED inputs under the configured root.
validation: Check one observation per assigned quarter, nonmissing values, date parsing and four-quarter lead/lag availability at both estimation endpoints.

review_notes: The scope is the complete supplied code.do program: Call Report and ancillary data construction, the main published-paper tables/figures, and the independent Figure 6 loan-loss-provision timing branch near the end. The companion reloads regmaster and char and separately merges the state index.

The 6,148-line final_log.smcl is historical output, not evidence of a current run and not a second program. The appendix reports OA tables/sections, but no separate appendix-specific executable workflow is supplied.
The final bank-quarter sample is created by code.do and is not packaged as an analysis-only input. No compatible prepared-sample route was verified.

The two Data-root resets in B and C are coherent: B writes Data/work files/sample and C sets its root to the project parent then reads Data/work files/sample. The remaining path issue is that author Dropbox roots and output directories need a host-visible [redacted-path-59bf254f867f] configuration.

regcoefs.xls is generated by putexcel matrices A1/B1 and read immediately with import excel without firstrow; it is not an external data dependency. Stata default column names A/B feed the Figure 6 calculations.
No author code was run and no regressions, data downloads, installations, source edits or result generation were performed.
